relevance.rationale: Companion to 0304010v1 (Ivanov-Olshanski) in this slice: Fulman reproves Kerov's character-ratio CLT by Stein's method and — the point — attaches an explicit error term, which the Kerov/Hora/Ivanov-Olshanski moment proofs do not have. QOU asserts convergence RATES (conj:jet-convergence-classical-limit's O(1/sqrt(k)); prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (2)'s O(1/sqrt(n-3))) without any source that states a rate. Fulman gives the q = 1 benchmark rate. Secondarily, his exchangeable pair is built from harmonic functions on Bratteli diagrams, which is the same combinatorial object as prop:wedderburn-bratteli-recursion. Supporting rather than core: it is q = 1 and the corpus's claims are q-deformed, so it calibrates rather than establishes them.

keyResults.statement: For n >= 2 and all real x_0, |P(((n-1)/sqrt(2)) chi^lambda(12)/dim(lambda) <= x_0) - Phi(x_0)| <= 40.1 n^{-1/4}, with a conjectured C n^{-1/2}.
keyResults.useForFolio: The only explicit Berry-Esseen rate for the Plancherel character-ratio CLT. Gives a concrete q = 1 number against which the corpus's asserted O(1/sqrt(k)) / O(1/sqrt(n-3)) rates can be sanity-checked, and shows the best proved distributional rate is n^{-1/4}, not n^{-1/2} — which is weaker than what the corpus's prose implies.

keyResults.statement: Coherence relation for measures on a Bratteli diagram: M_n(lambda) = sum_{lambda -> Lambda} (dim(lambda) kappa(lambda,Lambda)/dim(Lambda)) M_{n+1}(Lambda), with Plancherel measure on the Young lattice (kappa == 1) as the special case; the down-transition gives an exchangeable pair.
keyResults.useForFolio: The same down-transition structure prop:wedderburn-bratteli-recursion uses for Hecke Wedderburn blocks, stated in the general Bratteli-diagram form with the dim-ratio weights. Usable as the probabilistic reading of that recursion (coherent measures = harmonic functions), and as a source for the fact that this construction is what makes a CLT with error term possible.

keyResults.statement: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the Markov chain on partitions underlying the exchangeable pair, applied to the asymptotic decomposition of tensor powers of symmetric-group representations.
keyResults.useForFolio: The tensor-power decomposition asymptotics are the q = 1 shadow of the operator-valued branching combiner that Subgoal-1 names as the closure path for the per-isotope binding tower; a spectral description of the down-transition chain is a candidate structural input there. Flagged as a lead, not a wired result.

proposedActions.rationale: Clause (2) of prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton asserts a fluctuation rate with no rate-bearing source; Thm 1.2 is the q = 1 explicit rate.

Record that the best PROVED distributional rate for the q = 1 character-ratio CLT is n^{-1/4} (Fulman Thm 1.2), with n^{-1/2} only conjectured — so the corpus's O(1/sqrt(k)) prose is stronger than the q = 1 literature supports and needs restating or sourcing.
